LUNAFORGE – Engineering the Future of Space Exploration

LUNAFORGE is an interactive spacecraft engineering and space mission simulation platform that combines STEM education with engaging gameplay. Users design spacecraft by selecting engineering components and discover how their decisions directly affect mission performance.

Unlike traditional space games, LUNAFORGE connects engineering design to real gameplay mechanics. Spacecraft mass, battery capacity, solar generation, communication systems, cameras, and attitude control influence agility, energy reserves, boost recovery, scientific data collection, and mission efficiency.

The platform features dynamic space missions, asteroid hazards, three daily challenge types, an orbital sentinel boss, collectible scientific data cores, hidden discoveries, story transmissions, achievements, and a local leaderboard. Each mission ends with a detailed debrief showing performance and completed objectives. Users can then improve their spacecraft design and test it again.

LUNAFORGE makes complex engineering concepts accessible through hands-on experimentation. It develops critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and engineering decision-making while demonstrating how spacecraft subsystems work together. Our goal is to inspire students to explore STEM and become the next generation of space engineers and innovators.

Project Details – LUNAFORGE

LUNAFORGE is an interactive spacecraft engineering and space mission simulation platform that combines STEM education, engineering design, and space exploration gameplay. It allows users to design spacecraft by selecting different engineering components, then test their designs through dynamic space missions where every engineering decision has a measurable effect on performance.

How It Works

Users begin by designing a spacecraft and selecting components for essential systems, including power generation, battery storage, communication, onboard computing, cameras, and attitude determination and control. The platform evaluates the selected design and generates an engineering profile that directly influences gameplay. For example, spacecraft mass and attitude control affect maneuverability, battery capacity affects available energy and shield duration, solar generation influences boost recovery, and camera systems improve scientific data collection.

After completing the design stage, users enter interactive missions featuring asteroid hazards, collectible scientific data cores, environmental challenges, and an orbital sentinel boss. The platform also includes three daily challenge variations, hidden discoveries, story transmissions, achievements, and a local leaderboard. At the end of each mission, a detailed debrief presents the player's performance, collected data, discoveries, and completed objectives. Users can return to the builder, improve their spacecraft, and test a new design.

Benefits and Intended Impact

LUNAFORGE transforms abstract engineering concepts into practical, interactive experiences. It helps users understand how spacecraft subsystems interact and how engineering trade-offs influence mission success. It develops critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, decision-making, and systems engineering skills. Our intended impact is to make space engineering more accessible and exciting, especially for students interested in STEM, and to encourage them to explore careers in aerospace and related fields.

Tools and Technologies

The project was developed as a web-based application using:

  • JavaScript – core application logic and interactive systems.
  • React – component-based user interface and application structure.
  • HTML5 and CSS3 – interface layout, styling, and responsive design.
  • HTML Canvas – real-time space gameplay and visual interactions.
  • Local Storage – saving achievements, discoveries, and local flight records.
  • Git and GitHub – version control, collaboration, and project development.
  • Vercel – planned deployment and web hosting.

Creativity and Innovation

Our main innovation is connecting spacecraft engineering design to actual mission behavior instead of treating design as a separate theoretical activity. A spacecraft is not simply assigned a score; its selected components influence how it moves, manages energy, collects data, and survives challenges. We also combine engineering simulation with mission-based storytelling, daily challenges, boss encounters, discoveries, and performance feedback to create an educational experience that is both engaging and meaningful.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered scientific relevance, engineering trade-offs, usability, accessibility, engagement, performance, and educational value. We aimed to make the experience understandable for beginners while preserving meaningful engineering decisions. We also considered the importance of feedback and replayability, allowing users to learn from mission outcomes, modify their spacecraft, and improve their designs through experimentation.
